subject: TheraBright — derivative log sampling & erasure playbook request
body:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@therabright.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: security@therabright.com, procurements@therabright.com
Date: 2027-11-28 09:12 AM PST
Subject: Data derivative logs and erasure: initial ask

Hi Monica,

We are reviewing our SIG/SOC2 attachments and have a couple of items we'd like to align on for integration testing ahead of contract signature. Specifically:

1) For requests to fully delete a tenant's customer data, what gets erased beyond direct PII? We need clarity on derivative artifacts (aggregated logs, sampled usage telemetry, aggregated model prompts that may contain PII fragments) and whether TheraBright can request a tenant-scoped purge.

2) For cases where we ask for a targeted erasure (e.g., subset of user identifiers), do you provide a playbook and attestation that derivative artifacts are either removed or irreversibly anonymized? We have internal legal and privacy requirements for a documented MOP and an SLA for completion.

Could you share the playbook, expected timelines, and any caveats (forensic hold, backup retention windows, log sampling policies)? I'll attach our SIG matrix and mark the rows where we need evidence.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Security, TheraBright

---

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@therabright.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-28 11:30 AM PST
Subject: Re: Data derivative logs and erasure: initial ask

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Neha (security engineering) and Rishi (compliance) to draft a playbook and confirm bounds. Quick answers up-front:

- We support tenant-scoped deletion requests; core customer data + primary session logs are removable subject to legal/forensic holds.
- Derivative artifacts: default behavior differs by artifact type. Aggregated telemetry (daily aggregates) are retained for 90 days then downsampled; sampled prompt traces and ephemeral KV caches are purged on delete, but we need to validate examples in your SIG matrix.
- Timeline: standard erasure for a tenant (no holds) typically completes in 7–14 business days; extended if backups, third-party snapshots, or legal holds are present.

Neha — can you prepare a draft playbook (MOP + attestation language) and annotate the list of artifacts we can fully delete vs. those we can only anonymize? Also include required inputs from TheraBright (exact tenant id, list of internal user IDs, signed SLA acceptance).

Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

---

On Mon, Nov 29, 2027 at 08:45 AM, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Monica / Laura — attaching a preliminary MOP and artifact map. See key excerpts below; full docs attached: therabright_sig_matrix.xlsx, requested_artifacts_manifest.pdf.
>
> Summary (technical):
> - Primary session logs (per-request headers, timestamps, ephemeral KV) = deletable within 7 business days after we validate tenant identifiers and outstanding investigations.
> - Aggregated telemetry (rollups used for performance metrics) = retained at 90 days; we can provide a one-time targeted downsample-and-redact for older buckets but not retroactively remove from published aggregates without potential metric gaps.
> - Prompt traces (text that entered the model) = stored encrypted; by default we retain raw traces for 30 days, after which they are redacted to remove tokens matching high-risk patterns (PII regexes). We can perform tenant-scoped full-trace deletion for records that are still within retention windows.
> - Backups and immutable snapshots: restorations may reintroduce deleted artifacts until snapshot TTLs expire. Backup retention window: 60 days for critical snapshots; to accelerate deletion across snapshots we recommend a snapshot sweep request (timeline ~14–30 days depending on scope).
>
> Inputs required from TheraBright to start an erasure:
> 1) Tenant identifier(s) + list of email hashes or user IDs to remove (CSV).
> 2) Signed erasure request form (DocuSign link, see related links).
> 3) Confirmation there are no active legal/forensic holds.
>
> Caveats & exceptions:
> - Forensic/Legal holds will pause automated deletion until lifted.
> - Some aggregated derivatives used for product safety (abuse signals, safety model training) are maintained in an irreversible hashed form for 180 days; we can provide attestations on hashing and access controls but cannot reconstruct original tokens.
>
> Next steps: Rishi, please add compliance attestation language and timelines; Jonas, please include ops steps for snapshot-sweep coordination.
>
> Neha Kapoor
> Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
>

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@therabright.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: security@therabright.com
Date: 2027-12-01 10:05 AM PST
Subject: Re: Data derivative logs and erasure: initial ask

Thanks, Neha — that helps a lot. A few follow-ups:

1) Can you provide a one-page attestation template we can store with our record of erasures? It should state exactly what was removed, the snapshot sweep status, and a timestamped completion statement signed by Redwood.
2) For aggregated telemetry that you can only downsample, we need language specifying how the downsample will prevent re-identification (method + parameters).
3) We will likely request a tenant-scoped purge plus a subset of individual user erasures for a compliance incident. Please confirm an SLA timeline if both are requested concurrently.

I'll also have our procurement/legal folks send a signed DocuSign once we finalize the attestation template.

Laura

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@therabright.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-02 04:20 PM PST
Subject: Re: Data derivative logs and erasure: initial ask

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. A few commitments and the operational playbook outline below: 

Commitments:
- Attestation: we will provide a timestamped attestation PDF for each erasure event. The attestation will list deleted artifact classes, snapshot sweep status, and a signed approval from our compliance team. Standard attestation turnaround: 2 business days after completion.
- SLA: concurrent tenant purge + subset user erasures = target 14 business days (subject to backup/snapshot sweep). We will escalate to a 10-business-day target for enterprise accounts with a dedicated SLT contact.

High-level playbook (MOP):
1) Intake & verification (Day 0–1): receive signed DocuSign request + CSV of tenant/user IDs. Verify ownership and absence of legal hold.
2) Pre-sweep snapshot check (Day 1–2): identify active snapshots that include the target data; schedule a snapshot sweep if requested.
3) Primary deletion pass (Day 3–7): remove live artifacts (session logs, prompt traces within retention window).
4) Snapshot sweep (Day 7–21): execute snapshot sweep and mark sweep completion. Timeline depends on snapshot count and storage vendor scheduling.
5) Post-deletion verification & attestation (Day 1–2 after completion): QA checks and generate attestation PDF.

Requested deliverables we will include:
- Signed attestation PDF
- CSV manifest of deleted record identifiers (hashed where necessary)
- Summary of any derivative artifacts retained and rationale + anonymization parameters

I've attached a draft attestation template (redaction_mop_v1.docx) and our suggested wording for SIG/SOC2 responses. If this looks good, Monica will coordinate legal/Procurement to accept the doc, and Neha/Jonas will schedule the ops runbook call.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Compliance & Risk, Redwood Inference
